references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 24:45|Matthew 24:45] contains the same parable about the faithful and wise servant whom the master puts in charge of his household to give them their food at the proper time. Luke uses the word 'steward' (οἰκονόμος) while Matthew has 'servant' (δοῦλος).

In the parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:21-23|Matthew 25:21-23], the master says to the faithful servant, "You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much." This expresses the same principle that faithfulness leads to greater responsibility.

Paul describes in [ref:1 Kor 4:1-2|1 Corinthians 4:1-2] the apostles as 'servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries,' emphasizing that what is required of stewards (οἰκονόμους) is that they be found faithful (πιστός). The same terminology appears in Luke 12:42.

In [ref:Tit 1:7|Titus 1:7], an overseer is referred to as 'God's steward' (θεοῦ οἰκονόμον), who must be blameless. This shows how the responsibility of a steward from Jesus' parable was applied in church leadership.
In [ref:1 Pet 4:10|1 Peter 4:10], believers are called 'good stewards of God's varied grace' (καλοὶ οἰκονόμοι), reflecting the ideal of stewardship that Jesus portrays in this parable.

In the parable of the dishonest manager in [ref:Luk 16:1-2|Luke 16:1-2], the same word (οἫκονόμος) is used for a manager who must give an account of his management. Both texts deal with the responsibility that comes from being placed over another's possessions.

The preceding exhortation in [ref:Luk 12:35-38|Luke 12:35-38] to be ready and watchful forms the immediate context for the question about the faithful steward. Peter's question in verse 41 leads into this parable, which expands on what it means to be prepared.

In [ref:Hebr 3:5-6|Hebrews 3:5-6], Moses is described as faithful (πιστός) in all God's house as a servant, while Christ is faithful as the Son over his own house. Faithfulness in stewardship is a recurring theme.
Joseph was appointed steward over Potiphar's house in [ref:1 Mos 39:4-6|Genesis 39:4-6], an Old Testament foreshadowing of the faithful steward whom the master sets over all he owns.

In [ref:Ordsp 25:13|Proverbs 25:13], a faithful messenger is compared to cooling snow in harvest time – it refreshes his master's soul. This illustrates the value of faithfulness in service, just as the faithful steward provides food at the proper time.
